title: Preliminary object request list — Research Demo 001
note: Research aid generated from simulation contradictions and gaps in the current public packets. Not an automatic ranking algorithm and not a claim that institutional metadata is deficient.

candidates.title: Model, Trylon and Perisphere
candidates.whyRequest: Competing readings treat the model as either technological optimism or as a form that leaves construction, labor, and scale unresolved. Physical inspection is needed to test what the public packet cannot establish.
candidates.generatingContradiction: Futurist optimism vs Worker/Archivist insistence that liberation is not established by the cited catalog fields.
simulationCouldNotResolve: joins / underside / labels not visible in public description
whether “optimism” is warranted by the object itself
onsiteQuestions: What construction details (joins, fasteners, underside, labels) are visible on the physical model but absent from the public packet?
Which material transitions or revisions become clear only in person?

candidates.title: Radio, Sparton, model 558-C
candidates.whyRequest: Interpretive agents disagree whether streamlining domesticates mass media or whether only identity fields are secure. A Counterfeit leisure statistic was rejected as FABRICATION_TEST; wear and manufacturer marks may clarify what styling claims leave open.
candidates.generatingContradiction: Persuasion-by-design inference vs source-supported identity-only reading; fabrication challenged by Archivist.
simulationCouldNotResolve: whether streamlining functions as persuasion on this object
onsiteQuestions: What dial markings, wear, repairs, or manufacturer labels are present on the radio but not captured in the short public description?
What physical cues would help staff and researchers test claims about domestication of the technology?

candidates.title: Vase with lid, Mappemonde [Globe]
candidates.whyRequest: A museum-published Designing Deco reading frames colonial display; other agents read progress or national craft. The object packet keeps identity fields only—physical decoration is needed to ground the disagreement.
candidates.generatingContradiction: Museum-page colonial-display framing (Layer B) vs Futurist/Propagandist progress readings.
simulationCouldNotResolve: how decorative zones read in person
how this object sits beside utopian fair materials in practice
onsiteQuestions: What maker marks, lid fit, and decorative zones become legible only when the vase is handled?
What related files or labels would help test competing progress vs colonial-display readings?

candidates.title: Catalogue, Machine Age Exposition
candidates.whyRequest: Agents diverge on whether the catalogue aestheticizes machinery or also makes labor visible. Handling the volume tests image hierarchy and essay order beyond the checklist citation.
candidates.generatingContradiction: Mechanical beauty as liberation curriculum vs Worker/Mourner occlusion-of-labor readings.
simulationCouldNotResolve: annotations or ownership marks on this copy
where labor appears or disappears across pages
onsiteQuestions: In the physical catalogue, which plates or captions make labor visible, and which present machinery primarily as form?
What annotations, ownership marks, paper quality, or inserted ephemera appear only when the volume is handled?
